items.text: collections are toggles, and one set: pick as many as you like in Scenes or in Auto play (they are the same choice), and the robot plays what Scenes shows; All turns them all back on
a pin in each panel's band, beside ‹ ›: pinned, the panel stays up while you play on the stage; Close still closes it, and the pin is remembered

Pulse, a tab in the Sound panel: the field on the beat. Surge pushes the particles along their path (below zero it kicks them back), Breathe pulls them in toward the lines and lets them out, Sway swings the current side to side; with presets Heartbeat, Undertow, Lungs, Tide and Sway
the license asks you to credit what you make as “made with Current by CHAMY·XYZ”

the capture button says its mode by its dot, not a word on top of it: a white dot for a still, the red record dot for video, the red dot with a loop through it for a GIF, a white dot with its corner peeling for a sticker; the pills in its shelf wear the same marks
Morph counts in seconds, beats or bars, like Every, and has its own dice: each change draws a new length
Auto play's Collection chips sit last, under Morph, so Morph is on the screen without scrolling
the AI ratio, answered again: 79% human (execution 70, direction 88, ideas and research 85, curation 80, self 70), and the record recounted, 351 of 501 changes started from the artist's direction
the AI ratio card wears the index's own type, rules and accent, in light and dark, instead of the AI:RATIO brand colours
the picture's automation presets (Breathe, Drift, Slow turn…) are a row of pills that scrolls sideways, so the sliders they set stay on the screen; the lit one is what the sliders hold now

the small words under the bar (video under capture, mic under the speaker) carry their own ground in the bar's colours, so they read on any stage in light or dark, and step aside from a badge instead of printing over it
Room and Audience wear the open padlock at the end of their names in the index: both are Pro features, open to everyone in the beta
Audience is a Pro feature of its own, open to everyone in the beta (the open padlock on Let the audience in); joining from a phone stays free

Audience, in the index after Room. Let the audience in and the stage shows a code; phones scan it and every finger on every phone pulls the current, in that phone's color. With Water on, each phone plays the water sound it picked (drop, bubbles, whale, porpoise, gull) through this computer's speakers. Close the doors, lift every finger, push instead of pull, and cap how many phones. For now a rehearsal: phone windows on this computer (a phone window opens one), until the audience relay goes online
